vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: executive-assistant-time-blocking
Version: 1.0.0

The skill defines a structured workflow for an AI agent to act as an executive assistant, managing tasks and calendar events using the 'gog' CLI tool. The instructions in SKILL.md outline a logical process for task retrieval, urgency assessment, and automated scheduling with verification loops (Jidoka) to prevent overlaps. No indicators of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized command execution were found.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (autonomously scheduling incomplete tasks into Google Calendar) matches its instructions and requirements, but it will act on your existing calendar credentials and can create/delete events — you should review and test before letting it run autonomously.

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly uses a CLI named 'gog' to list Google Tasks and read/create/delete Google Calendar events, which aligns with a time‑blocking assistant. The declared required binary (gog) matches the commands referenced in SKILL.md. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrowly focused on task collection, estimating durations/urgency, retrieving calendar events, gap analysis, and creating/deleting calendar events. However, the workflow performs potentially destructive actions (deleting/rescheduling events) and does not include explicit user confirmation, a dry‑run mode, or scoping of which calendars/events are safe to modify. It also assumes the 'gog' CLI is already authenticated and will use whatever account access is available.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or external downloads are included—this is instruction-only. That minimizes disk-write/install risk; the skill will only invoke the 'gog' binary that must already be present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, which is coherent. But it implicitly relies on existing local authentication for the 'gog' CLI (e.g., stored OAuth tokens/config), which gives the skill access to the user's calendars. There is no explicit scoping or guidance about which Google account or calendar 'primary' refers to.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request system persistence. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default), so if the agent is permitted to call skills autonomously it can run this workflow and modify calendars — expected for an assistant skill but worth noting because of the create/delete actions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will use your installed 'gog' CLI and whatever Google credentials that CLI already has to read tasks and modify your calendar (create and delete events). Before enabling it: 1) Verify the 'gog' binary is the legitimate tool you expect and that it is authenticated to the correct Google account. 2) Test with a dry-run or a non-primary/test calendar if possible to observe planned changes without committing them. 3) Ensure you are comfortable with automatic deletion/rescheduling behavior or add a manual confirmation step. 4) Back up important calendar data (export) before first use. If you need higher assurance, ask the skill author to add an explicit dry-run mode, per-event confirmation, and calendar scoping options.
